headline: BoC Holds at 2.25% as Canada Adds 14,000 Jobs in March and February Trade Deficit Widens to $5.7B on Record Imports

facts.statement: Bank of Canada held the policy interest rate at 2.25% on March 18, 2026, the seventh consecutive decision at this level. The Summary of Governing Council Deliberations published in April noted the US Supreme Court's Feb 20 ruling on IEEPA tariffs had 'no direct implications for sectoral tariffs on Canadian exports' and 'trade-related risks to Canada remained unchanged.' The next Fixed Announcement Date is April 29, 2026.
facts.source_title: Bank of Canada — Policy rate statement, March 18, 2026
connections: 217 residential projects ($44.4B) in the database are sensitive to borrowing costs
2213 infrastructure projects ($182.4B) also rate-linked via project finance
GoC 2Y yield at 2.79% sits 54bp above the overnight rate, signaling the market prices rates on hold through mid-year

facts.statement: Canada added 14,000 jobs in March 2026, partially reversing February's -84,000 decline. The unemployment rate held at 6.7%, the employment rate at 60.6%, and the participation rate at 64.9%. Average hourly wages grew 4.7% year-over-year, up from 3.9% in February — the fastest pace since October 2024. Year-over-year, 87,100 more Canadians were employed than in March 2025.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — Labour Force Survey, March 2026
connections: 1031 projects currently Under Construction depend on labour market capacity
217 residential projects and 2213 infrastructure projects are the largest labour-intensive categories
Wage acceleration to 4.7% Y/Y runs 290bp above headline CPI at 1.8% Y/Y

facts.statement: Canada's merchandise trade deficit widened to -$5.7B in February 2026, the largest since August 2025, as imports set an all-time record of $72.1B (+8.4% M/M). Exports rose to $66.3B (+6.4% M/M), highest since March 2025, with increases in 9 of 11 product sections. Motor vehicles and parts exports rebounded +24.2% after January's -21.2% drop; metal and non-metallic mineral imports rose +45.6% on gold shipments.
facts.value: -$5.7B deficit; $72.1B record imports; +24.2% motor vehicle exports
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — Canadian international merchandise trade, February 2026
connections: 61 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) linked to energy export flows
48 manufacturing projects ($67.4B) tied to motor vehicle and parts trade
362 mining projects ($159.5B) linked to metals and minerals trade

facts.statement: The Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed through early April despite a US-Iran ceasefire announced around April 8. Shipping was reported 'at a standstill' with Iran charging tolls reported above US$1 million per vessel. The strait normally handles approximately 20% of global seaborne oil and gas flows. WTI traded near US$98/bbl on April 10 after closing at US$102.18/bbl on March 31; Brent traded in the US$98-105 range.
facts.source_title: Al Jazeera — Shipping in Strait of Hormuz at a trickle despite US-Iran ceasefire
connections: 61 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) in the database are directly linked to crude price conditions
806 power and energy projects ($507.7B) are linked to global energy pricing via LNG and offtake
BoC Governing Council flagged the energy shock as a source of near-term inflation pressure in its March deliberations

facts.statement: Headline CPI ran at +1.8% Y/Y in February 2026, down from +2.3% in January — the lowest since early 2021. Core measures converged around the 2% target: CPI-median 2.3%, CPI-trim 2.3%, CPI-common 2.4%. Food inflation decelerated to 5.3% from 7.3%. The March CPI release is scheduled for April 20.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — Consumer Price Index, February 2026
connections: Headline CPI at 1.8% sits 45bp below BoC's 2.25% overnight rate, implying positive real policy rate
Core measures within BoC's 1-3% control range
Wage growth of 4.7% Y/Y runs 290bp above headline CPI

facts.statement: Canadian real GDP rose +0.1% in January 2026, a second consecutive monthly increase. Goods-producing industries +0.2%; mining, quarrying, oil and gas extraction +1.2% (oil and gas extraction +1.6%); construction +1.1% M/M; manufacturing -1.4% (steepest monthly decline in current cycle). The advance estimate for February is +0.2%. The February GDP release is scheduled for April 28.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — Gross domestic product by industry, January 2026
connections: 48 manufacturing projects ($67.4B) linked to the -1.4% M/M manufacturing GDP print
61 oil and gas projects aligned with the +1.6% monthly oil and gas extraction increase

cross_references.interpretation: The policy rate hold keeps borrowing costs stable for 217 residential and 2213 infrastructure projects ($226.8B combined) in the database. The GoC 2Y at 2.79% prices a mid-year continuation of the hold.

The -1.4% January manufacturing GDP print — the steepest monthly decline in the current cycle — maps onto 48 manufacturing projects ($67.4B) in the database. February merchandise trade data showed motor vehicles and parts exports rebounding +24.2%, which may reverse some of the weakness.

WTI declined from $102.18/bbl (Mar 31) to ~$98/bbl (Apr 10) as Strait of Hormuz flows remain near zero. The database tracks 61 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) and 806 power and energy projects ($507.7B).

February imports reached a record $72.1B. Metals and minerals imports rose +45.6% on gold shipments; motor vehicle and parts exports rebounded +24.2%. The widening deficit is linked to projects across oil & gas, manufacturing, mining, and transport/logistics in the database.
The 1031 projects Under Construction in the database depend on available labour. Wage growth of 4.7% Y/Y runs 290bp above headline CPI (1.8%), increasing real labour costs for those projects.
February housing starts at 250,900 SAAR, up 4.5% from January. The database tracks 217 residential projects ($44.4B). CMHC's March release is scheduled for April 17.

key_developments: March CPI released April 10: headline +0.9% M/M / +3.3% Y/Y, highest annual since May 2024, driven by +10.9% energy (gasoline +21.2%). Services ex-energy +0.2% M/M / +3.0% Y/Y.

March nonfarm payrolls +178,000 (vs. consensus +59,000; February revised to -133,000). Unemployment fell to 4.3% from 4.4%, partly from labour-force exit. Average hourly earnings +3.5% Y/Y, slowest since May 2021.
Federal Reserve held target range at 3.50-3.75% on March 18. Next FOMC meeting April 28-29 (Powell's final FOMC as Chair; term ends May 2026).
S&P 500 closed April 10 at 6,816.89 (+3.6% week, best since November) after the prior week's ~9% drop (worst week since March 2020) triggered by the April 2 tariff announcement.

US Supreme Court voided IEEPA tariffs on February 20 (Learning Resources v. Trump). Trump replaced them with a 10% global import surcharge, with CUSMA-originating goods exempt. Section 232 tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminum, autos, and softwood lumber remain in force under separate statute.
global_package.canada_impact: The Fed-BoC policy rate spread of 125-150bp keeps CAD/USD near 0.7200. US March CPI reacceleration to 3.3% raises cross-border inflation transmission risk. Canadian motor vehicle and parts exports rebounded +24.2% in February following the January -21.2% drop, but Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum, autos, and softwood lumber remain in force despite the IEEPA ruling. Up to US$175B in IEEPA-era tariff refunds are projected (Penn Wharton).

key_developments: ECB held all three key rates at the March 19 meeting: deposit facility 2.00%, main refinancing 2.15%, marginal lending 2.40%.
ECB March projections raised the headline inflation path: 2.6% average 2026, 2.0% 2027, 2.1% 2028 — upward revision on Middle East energy assumptions.
Euro area Q4 2025 GDP +0.2% Q/Q; HICP +1.9% Y/Y (below 2% target); unemployment 5.9%.
Germany recorded a second consecutive annual GDP contraction.
Next ECB Governing Council meeting April 30.
global_package.canada_impact: ECB deposit rate (2.00%) sits 25bp below BoC overnight (2.25%). The euro strengthened toward 1.1460 EUR/USD at end-March. CETA governs Canada-EU trade; the German contraction dampens European demand for Canadian resource exports. The Strait of Hormuz closure has introduced energy and shipping cost pressures across the eurozone.

key_developments: BoE MPC held Bank Rate at 3.75% unanimously on March 18.
UK CPI +2.8% Y/Y in February (above 2% target); preliminary estimates suggest CPI running 3.0-3.5% over the next two quarters on higher energy prices.
Q4 2025 GDP +0.1% Q/Q; unemployment 5.2%.
Next MPC decision and Monetary Policy Report April 30. ~90% of polled respondents expect a hold at 3.75%; 5 expect a 25bp hike.
global_package.canada_impact: BoE-BoC policy rate spread of +150bp reflects persistent UK inflation versus Canada's declining trajectory (1.8% Y/Y). UK-Canada trade operates under CPTPP. The Strait of Hormuz closure elevates UK energy import costs (UK is a net energy importer).

global_package.canada_impact: China is Canada's second-largest merchandise trading partner (~5% of merchandise exports). The return to manufacturing expansion supports demand for Canadian crude, canola, potash, wood products, and seafood. Higher shipping costs from Strait of Hormuz closure affect Canadian LNG and commodity routes to Asia. Steel prices rose 6.6% week on China PMI recovery (SLX +76.3% Y/Y); Nutrien/potash down 2.8% week.
